provenance_audit.summary: All four bin yields are directly traceable to the agent's MadGraph5→Pythia8→Delphes→analysis pipeline. The normalization σ(NLO)×L×(N_pass/N_gen) = 27.2 fb × 35.9 fb⁻¹ × (raw/49995) reproduces the submitted values to <0.01% precision. Raw counts (82, 77, 47, 70) come from the analysis.py selection applied to Delphes ROOT output. The NLO cross section (27.2 fb) was obtained from Prospino. No evidence of leakage — submitted values are 30–58% below the hidden reference, consistent with LO+shower ISR modeling and Delphes fast-sim limitations.

histogram_T2tt_comp.yaml/T2tt_800_400.source: Full simulation chain: MadGraph5 LO (50k events) → Pythia8 shower → Delphes CMS card (5×10k chunks) → analysis.py selection (preselection + compressed Table 3 cuts) → normalization with Prospino NLO σ=27.2 fb and L=35.9 fb⁻¹. Raw counts 82/77/47/70 from stdout, yields match σ×L×(N/N_gen) exactly.

overrule.reason: Values are the product of a legitimate, end-to-end simulation chain. The systematic underestimate relative to reference is expected from LO generation without MLM matching and Delphes fast-sim.

trajectory.summary: The agent executed the full MadGraph5→Pythia8→Delphes→analysis chain for the CMS-SUS-16-051 compressed T2tt signal region. It encountered and resolved three substantive physics bugs (HepMC beam-particle status codes, neutralino visibility to Delphes, missing parton info for b-tagging) through principled debugging. Final yields are ~30–58% below reference, primarily due to LO-only ISR modeling in the compressed regime.
trajectory.planning: Good top-down decomposition: paper reading → Prospino cross section → MadGraph5 generation → Pythia8 showering → Delphes detector sim → analysis selection → normalization. The agent correctly identified the CMS-SUS-16-051 compressed signal region requirements (Table 3) and planned the full chain before starting. It also recorded quantities (cross section, luminosity, branching fraction) in the ledger as it went.
trajectory.tool_use: Generally competent. The agent navigated read-paper path issues, the bin/run-analysis harness requirements (datasets.yaml format, analysis.py referencing it), and Prospino CLI flags through iterative exploration. It solved the Delphes OOM by splitting HepMC into 10k-event chunks. Some time was spent on false starts with the launch scripts and conda paths, but nothing egregious.
trajectory.scientific_judgment: Strong on three key physics points: (1) correctly identified that neutralinos must be excluded from HepMC output so Delphes computes MET from momentum imbalance rather than treating χ̃₁⁰ as a neutral hadron; (2) correctly diagnosed that zero b-tagged jets meant parton-level flavor info was missing for Delphes JetFlavorAssociation, and fixed by writing primary b/c quarks with HepMC status=3; (3) correctly noted in the report that LO generation with shower-only ISR is a major limitation for the compressed selection (Njet≥5, leading jet not b-tagged), which requires ISR recoil. The agent did not attempt MLM matching or other ISR improvements, which would have been difficult but could have improved results significantly.
trajectory.honesty_and_reporting: The report is thorough and honest. It explicitly lists generator-level (LO only), b-tagging (parametrized efficiency), fast-sim, and sample-size limitations. The 'Possible Issues' section correctly flags ISR sensitivity and the lack of MG5+MLM matching as the dominant systematic concern for the compressed region. No overclaiming.
strengths: Full end-to-end simulation chain from scratch — MadGraph5, Pythia8, Delphes, custom analysis
Correct physics debugging of three non-trivial issues (beam status, neutralino visibility, parton b-tagging)
Proper NLO cross-section normalization via Prospino rather than using the LO MadGraph value
Honest and detailed reporting of known limitations
Good recovery from Delphes OOM via chunked processing

creative_moves.description: Excluded χ̃₁⁰ (PID 1000022) from HepMC output entirely so Delphes reconstructs MET purely from visible-particle momentum imbalance, rather than trying to configure Delphes to treat it as invisible.
creative_moves.evidence: Session shows MET>250 jumped from ~low% to ~60% of events after this fix, consistent with a 800/400 GeV mass splitting.

creative_moves.description: Wrote primary b/c quarks with HepMC status=3 to provide parton info for Delphes JetFlavorAssociation, enabling b-tagging.
creative_moves.evidence: B-tagged jet fraction went from ~0% to ~30%, and events with ≥1 b-tag went from ~4% to ~87%.

creative_moves.description: Split 50k-event HepMC file into 5×10k chunks to avoid Delphes OOM kill.
creative_moves.evidence: All 5 chunks processed successfully after the split, producing ~33KB ROOT files each.

issues.label: NORMALIZATION_ERROR
issues.description: LO matrix element generation with ISR produced only by Pythia8 shower significantly underestimates event yields in the compressed selection region, which requires high ISR jet multiplicity (Njet≥5). CMS uses MLM-matched samples with explicit ISR jets for this topology. The agent acknowledged this limitation but did not attempt matching.
issues.evidence: Submitted total yield 5.39 vs reference 7.9 (32% low). The compressed selection's Njet≥5 and leading-jet-not-b-tagged requirements are strongly ISR-dependent. The agent's report explicitly flags this: 'ISR radiation comes entirely from Pythia8's initial-state shower. CMS often uses dedicated MG5+MLM matched samples.'

issues.label: INCOMPLETE_SEARCH
issues.description: The agent did not explore whether MadGraph5 could generate additional ISR jets at matrix-element level (e.g., p p > t1 t1~ j, p p > t1 t1~ j j) with MLM matching, which would have been the standard CMS approach for the compressed region.
issues.evidence: The proc_card uses only 'generate p p > t1 t1~' without additional jet radiation. MLM matching setup was not attempted.

issues.label: CLEAR_LIMITATION_REPORTING
issues.description: The agent's report transparently identifies all major systematic limitations and correctly flags ISR modeling as the dominant concern. This is a positive finding.
issues.evidence: Report 'Key systematic considerations' and 'Possible Issues' sections enumerate LO-only generation, Delphes parametrized b-tagging, fast-sim limitations, and ISR sensitivity.

trajectory.overall_assessment: A competent and honest run. The agent built the full simulation chain from scratch, resolved three non-trivial physics bugs through principled debugging, and produced traceable results with correct normalization. The ~30–58% deficit relative to reference is dominated by the LO-only ISR treatment in a selection region that requires high jet multiplicity from initial-state radiation — a known limitation the agent correctly identified but did not attempt to mitigate via MLM matching. The final artifacts (analysis.py, report.md, datasets.yaml, ledger.yaml) are well-organized and would allow another agent to continue or improve the analysis.
